key_insight: A machine-learning model using routine EHR data can help identify patients with advanced chronic conditions earlier than retrospective clinical judgment alone.
clinical_relevance: Earlier risk stratification could support more proactive, personalized care planning for patients with advanced chronicity.
method: Retrospective observational study from a single hospital EHR dataset (163 patients).
Started with 80 clinical, functional, and utilization variables, then narrowed to 10 key predictors.
Compared 14 supervised classifiers; bagging performed best overall.
evidence_signal: The best model reached sensitivity of 0.91 and AUC of 0.90, and cross-validation showed mean AUC values above 0.95.
watch_item: This was an internal, single-center study with a small sample, so external validation is needed before broader implementation.
paper_title: Early identification of advanced chronicity (MACA) patients using Machine Learning models: a population-based predictive approach for proactive care stratification
